clue.text: Lines for every single infringement

parts.note: BR, British Rail, stands for railway lines
each means for every single one

explanation.surface: A regulation forbids lines for each and every separate violation.
explanation.walkthrough: BR (British Rail, the old UK state railway) is the crossword's usual source for 'lines'.
explanation.definitionFit: A breach is a violation of a rule, contract or law.

clue.text: Outbreak of crimes, in outskirts of Bath, brings dishonour

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters between the edges of Bath
outskirts are the edges, so the first and last letters of Bath
an outbreak scatters things, so the letters of crimes break apart and re-form

explanation.surface: A crime wave on the edge of Bath shames the city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outbreak' suggests disease but signals the anagram; Bath is an English spa city, whose edges supply the outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To besmirch is to sully someone's reputation, a synonym of disgrace.

clue.text: Takes on commissions

explanation.surface: Someone accepts jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: Engages means hires or takes on staff, and also means commissions, as in engaging an architect.

clue.text: You are not encouraged to pick up this player's tricks

definitions.text: You are not encouraged to pick up this player's tricks

parts.words: You are not encouraged to pick up this player's tricks
parts.note: sounds like advice about copying a performer's skills, but tricks are also the hands won at cards, and this player's are won by cheating

explanation.surface: Warning against learning a certain performer's tricks.
explanation.definitionFit: A card cheat is a swindler who wins at card games by sleight of hand.

clue.text: Career direction 'in a dusty sport

parts.note: to career is to rush along, so the noun means rapid pace
a way is a route or direction

explanation.surface: A racer's career path takes them into a sport played in the dust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Career' is not a job here but headlong motion. Speedway is motorcycle racing on a loose cinder or shale oval, hence dusty.
explanation.definitionFit: Speedway racing kicks up clouds of cinders and shale as bikes slide round the oval track.

clue.text: The old man is top chap in there, surprisingly

indicators.note: surprisingly means the letters turn up in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: The old fellow turns out to be the head man in there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The old man' is not one's father but early, fossil man.
explanation.definitionFit: Pithecanthropus was the former name for Java Man, an extinct early human, so the word means ape-man of long ago.

clue.text: Strangely frightening energy in lake

indicators.note: in places the energy symbol inside the lake

parts.note: Erie is one of the North American Great Lakes
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: An eerie energy hangs over the lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Eerie means uncanny, weird enough to cause unease.

clue.text: Making for western terminal.

parts.note: a terminal is an end, an ending

explanation.surface: Heading for the western bus station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terminal' looks like a station but is used as an end or ending.
explanation.definitionFit: Wending one's way means travelling towards a destination.

clue.text: The old sign of those not quite gentlemen?

parts.note: ye is an archaic spelling of the
an omen is a sign or portent

explanation.surface: An archaic signal identifying men just below the gentry?
explanation.walkthrough: Historically yeomen were small freeholding farmers, ranking just below the gentry.
explanation.definitionFit: Yeomen were landowning commoners, a rank beneath the gentry in old English society.

clue.text: Plant with runners —- layer with yellow sulphur

parts.note: a hen is an egg layer
and means with, together with
yellow means cowardly, which is chicken
S is the chemical symbol for sulphur

explanation.surface: A runner plant covered in yellow sulphur powder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'layer' is not a stratum but something that lays eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a name for houseleeks and similar plants that spread by sending out small offsets on runners.

clue.text: But it does not come up with a cube root!

definitions.text: But it does not come up with a cube root!

parts.words: But it does not come up with a cube root!
parts.note: a crop dug from the field is a root, yet the sweetener refined from it ends up as cubes, not the other way about; the maths phrase cube root is the misdirection

explanation.surface: A mathematical quip about something failing to produce a cube root.
explanation.definitionFit: This field crop is a fleshy root grown to make the white crystals sold in lumps for tea.

clue.text: Rook advanced to carry out repetitive movement

parts.note: R is the chess abbreviation for rook
on means forward, advanced
to do is to carry out

explanation.surface: A chess rook moves forward to make a recurring manoeuvre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Movement' is musical: a section of a symphony or concerto, not a chess move.
explanation.definitionFit: A rondo is a musical piece or section whose main theme keeps recurring between episodes.

clue.text: Laughingly announced a nutritional intake

definitions.note: a plural Latin noun used for things taken in as food

indicators.note: announced signals that the phrase is to be heard, not spelt

parts.note: said laughingly means said in jest

explanation.surface: Someone jokingly declares a dietary figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'announced' turns IN JEST into its sound-alike INGEST; the clue's 'a' then adds A.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingesta is the physiologist's term for food and drink taken into the body.

clue.text: Recluse puts clock back, within limits of exactitude

indicators.note: within places the turned clock between the letters taken from exactitude
limits are the boundaries, so the first and last letters of exactitude
puts back means the word for clock is turned round

parts.note: a timer is a clock

explanation.surface: A hermit, seeking precision, sets his clock back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'puts clock back' sounds like the end of summer time, but it reverses the word for a clock; 'limits' are the first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An eremite is a hermit, a religious solitary living apart from society.

clue.text: Damages a rib?

parts.note: damage, as in what's the damage, is slang for the price, so cost

explanation.surface: A broken rib costs someone compensation?
explanation.walkthrough: COSTA is Latin, and the anatomist's word, for a rib; the question mark flags that unusual sense.
explanation.definitionFit: In anatomy costa is the formal Latin term for a rib, as in intercostal muscles.

clue.text: Single ad moved truck

indicators.note: moved means the letters are shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: A lone advert relocated a lorry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'truck' is not a lorry but dealings, as in 'have no truck with'.
explanation.definitionFit: Truck in the old sense means trade or business, so having truck with someone means having transactions with them.

clue.text: Lady Smitton announced

parts.note: reads like a footman naming a guest, but heard as lady smitten it is a woman in love, the Italian word for a sweetheart

explanation.surface: A butler announces the arrival of a titled guest.
explanation.definitionFit: An inamorata is a woman who loves or is loved, a female sweetheart.

clue.text: Henry stuffy and very angry

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for henry, the unit of inductance
a stuffy room is airless

explanation.surface: Henry is stuffy and furious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Henry' is not a man but the unit of inductance, symbol H. 'Hairless' is British slang for livid.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang to go hairless means to lose one's temper completely.

clue.text: Picture biscuits straight from the oven

parts.note: snaps, as in ginger snaps, are crisp biscuits
food straight from the oven is hot

explanation.surface: A photo of freshly baked biscuits.
explanation.definitionFit: A snapshot is a quick informal photograph.

clue.text: Reason for infanta's visit — to see Hazel, say?

definitions.text: Reason for infanta's visit — to see Hazel, say?

parts.words: Reason for infanta's visit — to see Hazel, say?
parts.note: recalls the nursery rhyme in which the King of Spain's daughter comes to visit for the sake of a little tree bearing a silver nutmeg and a golden pear; Hazel is that kind of tree

explanation.surface: Asks why a Spanish princess came: to see a girl called Hazel?
explanation.walkthrough: An infanta is a Spanish princess. 'Hazel' looks like a girl's name but is the tree, an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A hazel is a tree bearing edible nuts, and in the old rhyme the king's daughter came to visit such a tree.

clue.text: What is redolent of ' Kilimanjaro, mainly?

indicators.note: of here means drawn from within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: What does Kilimanjaro chiefly smell of?
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'KilimanjARO, MAinly'.
explanation.definitionFit: A scent or fragrance is what something redolent gives off.

clue.text: Abroad, crocodile may be used in sketch

parts.note: abroad means out, out and about
a crocodile is a line of schoolchildren walking in pairs

explanation.surface: A drawing of an overseas crocodile.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'crocodile' is the British school term for a column of children walking two by two.
explanation.definitionFit: An outline is a rough sketch showing only the main shape.

clue.text: What, in cricketing terms, is the best means of defence?

definitions.text: What, in cricketing terms, is the best means of defence?

parts.words: What, in cricketing terms, is the best means of defence?
parts.note: a batsman defends his wicket with the wooden implement he holds, so the cricket reading answers the question in three short words, while the run-together word is a military barrier

explanation.surface: A cricket quiz question about how best to defend.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the batsman defends his wicket with the bat; the whole word is a barricade of felled trees.
explanation.definitionFit: An abatis is a defensive barrier of felled trees with sharpened branches pointing at the enemy.

clue.text: Drug discovered — it may be connected with a plant

definitions.text: Drug discovered — it may be connected with a plant

parts.words: Drug discovered — it may be connected with a plant
parts.note: a newly found medicine may well come from vegetable sources, so the adjective describing anything relating to plants fits it

explanation.surface: A newly found drug might derive from a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' looks industrial but is the green sort.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanic is an adjective meaning relating to plants or botany, as in botanic gardens.

clue.text: Difficulty on court for a number of players

explanation.surface: Trouble on the tennis court for a group of players.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as NO NET, it would be a problem for a tennis court; whole, it is a group of nine musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: A tennis court lacking its central mesh barrier is unplayable, while a nonet is a group of nine musicians.

clue.text: Nothing in duty-list for Chanticleer?

indicators.note: in places the zero inside the rota

parts.note: a roster is a list of duties
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Is there no rota slot for the cockerel?
explanation.walkthrough: Chanticleer is the cockerel of medieval fable, as in Chaucer's Nun's Priest's Tale.
explanation.definitionFit: Chanticleer is the traditional name of the cock in beast fables, so a male farmyard fowl.

clue.text: Act to hold one in Italian city

indicators.note: to hold means the act's word contains the numeral

parts.note: a turn is a performer's act
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A performance includes a single show in an Italian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Turin is the Piedmontese city in northern Italy, Torino to Italians.

clue.text: Mischievous chimpanzees, deprived of nice cuppas initially, play up

indicators.note: mischievous chimpanzees are unruly, so their letters are jumbled
deprived of says some letters are first taken away from the apes
initially means the first letters of nice and cuppas

explanation.surface: Naughty chimps, denied their tea, misbehave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deprived of' takes N and C (the first letters of 'nice cuppas', from 'initially') out of CHIMPANZEES; 'Mischievous' rearranges what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: To play up a point is to stress or highlight it.

clue.text: Peg to retire in elegant environment, rather attractive

indicators.note: environment means surroundings, so the elegant word goes round the other piece

parts.note: swish means smart, elegant

indicators.note: to retire is to go back, so the word for peg is read in reverse

parts.note: a tee is the peg a golf ball is set on

explanation.surface: A golfer's peg goes back into a smart setting, quite charming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peg' is the golfer's tee, not a clothes peg; 'to retire' reads it backwards and 'environment' wraps the elegant word round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweet means pleasing or charming, and the suffix -ish softens it to somewhat so.

clue.text: They can, knock down lots of people

definitions.text: They can, knock down lots of people

parts.words: They can, knock down lots of people
parts.note: reads like violent things felling crowds, but describes auctioneers' hammers knocking down lots, items sold to people

explanation.surface: Things capable of flooring crowds.
explanation.definitionFit: An auctioneer bangs a small hammer to signal a lot is sold, or knocked down.
